title: Redefining chronic pain models: What should we model?
title_zh: 重新定义慢性疼痛模型：我们应当模拟什么？
abstract: Chronic pain is generally defined as pain that persists or recurs for more than 3 months. However, its pathogenesis cannot be fully explained solely by ongoing tissue injury or inflammation. Conventional inflammatory and neuropathic pain models have greatly advanced our understanding of pain hypersensitivity and its underlying mechanisms. Clinically, many patients experience persistent pain despite minimal peripheral pathology. These observations underscore the need for experimental models that better reflect the mechanisms of pain chronification and recurrence. Recent advances in research on central sensitization, hyperalgesic priming, and latent sensitization support the view that chronic pain involves persistent neuroplastic changes. In some chronic pain conditions, these changes may persist even after the initial injury or inflammation has resolved, suggesting that chronic pain may involve a form of "pain memory" encoded within the nervous system. This review outlines the limitations of conventional pain models and focuses on persistent sensitization models, particularly hyperalgesic priming and latent sensitization. Considering chronic pain as a manifestation of persistent neuroplastic changes, we summarize the experimental features and pathophysiological significance and discuss their relevance to chronic pain conditions that are difficult to explain solely by ongoing inflammation or nerve injury, including nociplastic pain-related conditions. Finally, we argue that future chronic pain models should aim to reproduce persistent neural states that drive pain chronification, maintenance, and recurrence rather than pain hypersensitivity alone. This approach may help bridge the translational gap between preclinical and clinical pain research and facilitate the development of more effective therapies.
abstract_zh: 慢性疼痛通常被定义为持续或复发超过3个月的疼痛。然而，其发病机制不能仅通过持续的组织损伤或炎症来完全解释。传统的炎症性和神经性疼痛模型极大地推进了我们对疼痛过敏及其潜在机制的理解。临床上，许多患者在外周病理极小的情况下仍持续疼痛。这些观察强调了需要更能反映疼痛慢化和复发机制的实验模型。关于中枢敏化、痛觉过敏启动和潜在敏化的最新研究进展支持慢性疼痛涉及持续的神经可塑性改变的观点。在某些慢性疼痛状态中，即使初始损伤或炎症已消退，这些改变仍可能持续，提示慢性疼痛可能涉及一种编码在神经系统内的“疼痛记忆”。本综述概述了传统疼痛模型的局限性，并聚焦于持续敏化模型，特别是痛觉过敏启动和潜在敏化。将慢性疼痛视为持续神经可塑性改变的表现，我们总结了实验特征和病理生理意义，并讨论了它们与仅由持续炎症或神经损伤难以解释的慢性疼痛状况（包括痛感性疼痛相关条件）的相关性。最后，我们认为未来的慢性疼痛模型应旨在再现驱动疼痛慢化、维持和复发的持续神经状态，而不仅仅是疼痛过敏。这种方法可能有助于弥合临床前与临床疼痛研究之间的转化鸿沟，并促进更有效治疗的开发。
